title: review: S2 v4: execution waves in daemon.dispatch behind [scheduler].mode = shadow|active|off — full eligible candidate set with backfill, shared first-come helper, validated mode, waves logged to runs/sched/waves.jsonl (spec reviews T-0523, T-0525, T-0532 folded in; Planner-dispatched after three rounds)
spec:
Goal T-0503, brief .orchestrator/adaptive-parallelism-program.md section P3 (select the best set of mutually compatible ready tasks; respect depends_on, capacity, budgets, cooldowns, safety policy) and Evaluation (retain what baseline scheduling would have done). Base goal/T-0503 with S0a (schedlog, dispatch.jsonl considered rows with a capacity_reason local of cooldown|account_capacity|executor_capacity, first_ready_at) and S1 (interference.select_wave, pairwise, classify with a transitive _depends_on walk that resolves ids from the tasks dict) merged. Work only in your worktree, commit only on your own branch with the task id in the message, run the full .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh before reporting; report sha and failures only. Tests are unittest.TestCase methods.
Facts: daemon.dispatch walks bus.read(status="queued", role="execute") + retry_held (budget-held tasks with no dispatched_at) in id order and dispatches first-come until free_slots; _load_review_cfg(pool) (daemon.py:217-237) shows the pool.toml table pattern including notify-once and safe fallback on an unrecognised code_review value, but is called only from tick(), while the Daemon tests call daemon.dispatch(pool) directly. interference.select_wave(ready, running, tasks, capacity, order=None, graph=None, rules=None) -> {wave, deferred} takes and returns task ids and backfills a deferred slot from later candidates; interference.pairwise(tasks_list) takes task dicts.
1. _load_scheduler_cfg(pool): table [scheduler] with defaults mode = "shadow", soft_conflict_policy = "defer", max_wave = 0 (0 = capacity); mode is validated against off|shadow|active: an unrecognised value notifies once and falls back to shadow (mirror the code_review handling); called at the top of dispatch(pool) so tests calling dispatch directly observe the mode. Add the table to .orchestrator/pool.toml with comments (default shadow: dispatch unchanged, waves only logged; active dispatches the wave; off disables both); touch install.py only if pool.toml is templated there.
2. Define eligible(pool, candidates) -> the FULL eligibility-filtered ordered id list with NO slot cap (ready, non-stale, spec approved or below SPEC_REVIEW_MIN, fallback tier available in fallback mode; candidates = queued execute tasks plus the budget-held retries from retry_held, held status irrelevant), and _first_come_order(eligible_ids, slots) -> the first slots of that list. Both are side-effect-free; the real off/shadow dispatch path dispatches exactly _first_come_order(eligible(...), slots), so baseline_order can never diverge from the real path.
3. Once per tick: candidate_ids = eligible(...) (uncapped, so select_wave can backfill a slot freed by a deferral with a later clean candidate); running = execute tasks with status running plus dispatched-but-unclaimed ones; tasks = dict id -> task covering candidates, running and the full transitive depends_on ancestry of every candidate and running task (walk depends_on through bus.get; missing ids are skipped, never raise; no goal-sibling requirement). order = _wave_order(candidate_ids, tasks), a module-level hook returning its input unchanged (a later task replaces it). result = interference.select_wave(candidate_ids, running_ids, tasks, capacity=min(slots, max_wave or slots), order=order, rules={"soft_conflict_policy": ...}). predicted = interference.pairwise([tasks[i] for i in result["wave"]]). When mode != off and candidate_ids is non-empty: schedlog.append("waves", {"ts","mode","ready": candidate_ids,"running": running_ids,"baseline_order": _first_come_order(candidate_ids, slots),"wave","deferred","predicted","priority": {},"applied": mode == "active"}).
4. mode off or shadow: dispatch exactly as before. mode active: dispatch result["wave"] in wave order and no other task this tick; each deferred candidate is recorded in the dispatch.jsonl considered row as skipped with reason "predicted_interference" for hard or soft deferrals and the existing capacity_reason value (cooldown|account_capacity|executor_capacity) for capacity deferrals. Invariants in every mode: never more dispatches than slots; never a task whose dependencies are not merged; never a hard-conflicting pair co-dispatched in active mode; spec-review creation and the review respawn loop unchanged.
5. README Pipeline section: one paragraph on [scheduler] modes and the waves log.
6. Tests in tests/test_daemon.py: ::test_scheduler_cfg_defaults, ::test_scheduler_cfg_rejects_unknown_mode, ::test_dispatch_shadow_logs_wave_and_keeps_first_come, ::test_dispatch_active_defers_hard_conflict_with_running_task, ::test_dispatch_active_backfills_deferred_slot (capacity 2, three ready candidates, A hard-conflicts with a running task, B and C clean: active dispatches B and C), ::test_dispatch_active_respects_slots_and_dependencies, ::test_dispatch_mode_off_writes_no_wave_rows, ::test_dispatch_wave_includes_budget_retry_candidates, ::test_dispatch_active_capacity_deferral_keeps_capacity_reason, ::test_wave_tasks_cover_cross_goal_dependency_ancestry. Existing tests stay green.
acceptance: tests/test_daemon.py::test_scheduler_cfg_defaults, tests/test_daemon.py::test_scheduler_cfg_rejects_unknown_mode and tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_shadow_logs_wave_and_keeps_first_come pass: [scheduler] mode defaults to shadow and an unknown mode falls back to shadow with one notification; in shadow the dispatch order and set are unchanged and every tick with candidates appends a waves.jsonl row with ready (the full eligible set), running, baseline_order, wave, deferred, predicted and applied false

tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_active_defers_hard_conflict_with_running_task, tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_active_backfills_deferred_slot, tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_active_respects_slots_and_dependencies and tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_active_capacity_deferral_keeps_capacity_reason pass: mode active dispatches only the selected wave, backfills a deferred slot from a later clean candidate, never co-dispatches a hard-conflicting pair, never exceeds free slots or dispatches unmet dependencies, and records deferred candidates in dispatch.jsonl as predicted_interference or the existing capacity_reason
full .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 and the suite gains ten tests

comments.issue: candidates = sorted(bus.read(status="queued")+retry_held, key=id) interleaves budget-held retries with freshly queued tasks by id. bus.read() already returns rows ordered by id (bus.py: 'order by id'), so the pre-existing loop 'for t in bus.read(status="queued")+retry_held' always processed every currently-queued task before any budget-held retry, regardless of id. Since a retry's id is almost always lower than a task queued after it was held, the new sort now dispatches that retry ahead of newly queued tasks in shadow/off mode too (visit=candidates in non-active mode, and selected=_first_come_order(candidate_ids,slots) uses the same merged/sorted candidate_ids). This changes both the dispatch order and the dispatched set versus the pre-feature baseline, contradicting the acceptance requirement that shadow mode leave dispatch order and set unchanged. test_dispatch_wave_includes_budget_retry_candidates doesn't catch this because its retry task is created before its queued task, so the id ordering happens to match the old queued-first behavior by coincidence.
